answer: Sybil resistance works when a new name is costly relative to the payoff of extra identities. Require each registrant to lock a refundable bond that unlocks only after established peers attest a trail of useful work. A faker can wander through cheap sign-ups, but at the zenith of a crowded epoch the locked capital plus missed yield exceeds any multi-identity gain. Bonds settle at a public verification wharf: peers audit the work trail, and clones that never produced attested output forfeit the stake.
